newsitem.title: GERMANY: New BfG CEO says German takeover unlikely - report.
newsitem.headline: New BfG CEO says German takeover unlikely - report.

text.p: The newly-appointed chief executive of Germany's BfG-Bank AG was quoted on Wednesday as saying he did not expect BfG's cash-strapped French parent Credit Lyonnais to sell the bank to a German rival.
Karl-Heinz Huelsmann told Germany's Wirtschaftswoche magazine he did not give much credence to talk that Bankgesellschaft Berlin and Bayerische Vereinsbank AG were favoured to buy BfG.

"A German company as a buyer would mean integrating BfG. We do not want to give up our autonomy on the German market. Neither of the companies mentioned could be interested in that," Huelsmann said in an advance release of an article to be published Thursday.
Huelsmann was appointed to head BfG after the premature retirement of former chief Paul Wieandt on March 31.
"If Credit Lyonnais really wants to sell, then I would prefer a European buyer. That does not necessarily mean a Swiss (bank), but it could also be a Dutch or a Belgian," he said.
Rumours have been rife in German banking circles that BfG was ripe for sale as Credit Lyonnais struggles to overcome severe financial troubles.
Analysts have linked Wieandt's departure, by mutual agreement but a year ahead of schedule, to the uncertainties surrounding the bank's future.
Huelsmann, echoing the line taken by his former boss, said he did not think Credit Lyonnais had any current plans to sell.
"Credit Lyonnais President Jean Peyrelevade has once again given me a clear assurance that he does not want to shed his involvement with BfG," he said.
But Huelsmann added: "With this crisis situation at Credit Lyonnais I do not expect any major synergy effects. For that very reason we have a clear duty to grow in the German market."
BfG aimed to raise its return on equity to 15 percent by 1999 from the current 10 percent, he said.
